sentence: An implementer who follows R5 as written makes admin sessions expire after 30 minutes, because R5 covers every session; following R7 as written makes admin sessions expire after 15 minutes, so the admin session length is contradictory and cannot be built as both.
evidence: R5 (line 10): 'A session expires after 30 minutes without activity.' R7 (line 12): 'Admin sessions expire after 15 minutes without activity.' R4 (line 7): admins are users with the editor powers.

sentence: An implementer who follows the spec-panel row adds --output, as the row says; nothing in the document says spec-panel already has that flag or that adding it is wrong. The stale-premise claim depends on command.md, which is outside the document, so the outcome does not follow from the text.
evidence: Line 120 (spec-panel row): 'add `--output`; contract | fresh dir | none'. The claim that the command already has --output rests on a file not in the document.

sentence: An implementer who follows the D1 example builds a troubleshoot call with --output, but the document never says troubleshoot rejects --output or that a call with it fails; the troubleshoot row lists only no --fix, so no stated text is contradicted or made impossible.
evidence: Line 228: '/sc:troubleshoot "login fails" --unattended --output .dev/troubleshoot/login/'. Line 91 (troubleshoot row): 'troubleshoot | no `--fix` |'. The claim that INV-B:242 names no output flag is outside the document.

sentence: An implementer who follows WC-10 is required to split only calls longer than 5 minutes; no stated text asks for a 4.5-minute call, and AC-4.3 (240 s limit) can be met by splitting at 4 minutes, so the outcome of a failing 4.5-minute call needs an assumption the document does not make.
evidence: Line 68 (WC-10): 'must be split into waits of at most 4 minutes'; line 266 (decision row): '4 minutes leaves a margin under the 5-minute heartbeat cadence'; line 210 (AC-4.3): 'no single tool call exceeds 240 s'.

sentence: An implementer who follows WC-10 is not told to make a call of 4 to 5 minutes; a 4.5-minute call that delays a heartbeat depends on whether Orca uses heartbeat age, which the document leaves as an assumption, so the failure does not follow from the stated text.
evidence: Line 68 (WC-10): 'A command step that blocks a single tool call for longer than 5 minutes ... must be split into waits of at most 4 minutes'; line 68 evidence: 'Cadence is from the dispatch preamble, not a guide'; line 210 (AC-4.3) states the 240 s limit.

sentence: SA-2 makes an Orca mention in the contract file allowed, not required; an implementer who follows the stated text need not write an Orca command there, and then passes AC-C1, so the failure needs a choice the text does not demand.
evidence: Line 147 (SA-2): 'The only allowed mention of Orca in a changed command is as an example of a caller's question channel inside the contract file.' Line 172 (AC-C1): grep for orca(-ide) orchestration|worktree|terminal|agent in src/superclaude/core must print nothing. Line 167: a phase passes only when every common check passes.

sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text must build a nightly purge that deletes activity logs at 180 days (R3) and also one that keeps them only for 90 days (R15); the same logs aged 90 to 180 days must both be deleted and kept, so two stated texts contradict.
evidence: Line 9 (R3): 'Activity logs are kept for 180 days and then deleted by the nightly purge job.' Line 27 (R15): 'Activity logs are kept for 90 days to limit exposure of IP addresses.'

sentence: An implementer who follows the load row (report none, no contract) builds load.md with only the usage line fixed and no Unattended mode section; that build fails AC-1.1, which requires every command in sections 3.1-3.2 to have that section naming return-contract.yaml, and AC-1.2, which runs the contract check on load. Two stated texts contradict, so the acceptance check cannot pass as written.
evidence: Line 112 (load row, 3.2 table): 'none (see note)' under report, 'n/a' under resume, 'P1 (usage line only)'. Line 159 (P1): 'load (usage line only)'. Line 195 (AC-1.1): every command in sections 3.1-3.2 must have a '## Unattended mode' section naming return-contract.yaml. Line 196 (AC-1.2): 7.2 check on each P1 command. Line 183 (7.2 step 4): test -s <contract>. Line 265 (decision): 'a report file would be an unrequested addition'.

sentence: P0 asks for an Orca section in HOW-WE-WORK.md and a contract file in core, but it does not state any literal orca command text; an implementer who writes no such command passes AC-C1, so the failure needs an unstated choice and the finding's own condition ('only if the text includes a literal command') is not met by the document.
evidence: Line 158 (P0): 'add an Orca section to `HOW-WE-WORK.md` ... Write `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (section 2 rules plus a coordinator brief template ...)'. Line 147 (SA-2): contract-file mention allowed as an example. Line 172 (AC-C1): grep must print nothing.

sentence: An implementer who follows WC-5 cannot tell what to send for a zero-byte or unparseable contract, or for a blocked contract with an empty blocked_question; no stated text covers these states, so the outcome is undefined rather than shown to be wrong by the text.
evidence: Line 62 (WC-4): 'when blocked, `blocked_question`' with no non-empty rule. Line 63 (WC-5): '`--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists'. Line 183 (7.2 step 4): test -s <contract> and yaml parse; line 200 (AC-2.2): non-empty blocked_question asserted only for gate runs.
